body: Thanks for the tip! Will refactor that.
Thanks for the feedback! Just wondering how would `String::from_utf8(output.stderr).ok()` still propagate `None`? (I'm completely new, to Rust so probably it's newbie question.)
I totally stole that from the [Go module](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/f2cb529d1bd44f996ad60c2d27ae14d1f9ad44ba/src/modules/golang.rs#L54-L69). Should we change that there too?

I think this way makes a lot more sense but ultimately they both work.

Even though it's not the biggest of issues, I think I'll still open a PR for it. This way no one will copy that code again :)

whoops, I meant return. It's not propagating here, you are right :)

EDIT: You could write it either way, but if you had a `?` at the end you would need to wrap everything in `Some` because you would be returning a `String` and not an `Option<String>`. So the line would look like this: `Some(String::from_utf8(output.stderr).ok()?)`
Ah okay, but performance-wise it's the same right?

something like this is never gonna affect performance anyway, but the way I suggested should be more efficient unless Rust optimizes it because it only creates one `Option` (`.ok()` does this) while the way I described in my second comment creates two `Option`'s, one with the `.ok()` and another directly from the `Some` call.
